title: 11 Best small business phone systems for 2026
summary: Looking for a business phone, but don't know where to start? This guide covers the 11 best small business phone systems in depth.
body_markdown:
The best small business phone systems do more than give you a second number. The right one helps you answer calls faster, miss fewer customers, and keep your whole team on the same page.


With a great phone system, callers can reach the right person quickly. Or if no one can pick up, a text or an AI agent can step in. And anyone with access can open a customer’s thread and see every call, text, and voicemail, so nobody has to relay messages.


But not every provider can give you that.


After testing dozens of phone systems and evaluating them for ease of use, scalability, features, and integrations, we’ve narrowed it down to the best. Here’s a quick summary:


1. **Quo.** Best overall for small and growing teams that want unlimited calling and texting to the US and Canada, shared numbers, and a built-in AI voice agent.
2. **Google Voice.** Best for solo users and teams that already use Google Workspace, only need basic US calling and texting, and don’t mind the Workspace requirement.
3. **Ooma Office.** Best small business phone system that still supports legacy hardware like fax machines and overhead pagers.
4. **Grasshopper.** Best for solopreneurs and very small teams that want multi-digit number extensions.
5. **Nextiva.** Best for teams that want omnichannel communication.


##


Methodology: How we evaluated the top small business phone systems


**


We ranked the best small business phone systems after our market intel team signed up for free trials, contacted sales and support teams, and tested call reliability firsthand. Here’s what we weighed:


1. **Price.** We evaluated each plan’s cost and checked for hidden fees. Budget matters, but so does what you get for it. We looked for platforms that offer the most value at each price point.
2. **Features.** We looked for providers with base plans that include everything you need to get started without expensive add-ons. We prioritized platforms that pack the most useful features into their entry-level plans.
3. **Customer support.** We tested how quickly and effectively each provider’s support team responded to questions. Reliable help matters most when something goes wrong, so we prioritized platforms with responsive, accessible support across multiple channels.
4. **Call quality.** We evaluated call reliability and uptime through firsthand testing on each platform. A poor call experience reflects on your business, so we only recommend providers that consistently deliver clear, stable connections.
5. **Scalability.** We looked at whether plans cap minutes or messages and whether essential features like call recording or shared numbers are locked behind upgrades. We favored platforms that can grow with your team without forcing costly plan upgrades.

Here’s a quick look at how each provider stacks up:

##


**Breaking down the best small business phone systems**


Investing in a business phone system is essential for building strong customer relationships, providing excellent customer support, and growing your business. Here are 11 of the best small business phone systems to consider:


### **1. **Quo: The best business phone system for small business****


Quo, formerly OpenPhone, is a[cloud-based phone system](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-cloud-phone-system/) for small and growing businesses. It lets you work together as a team from a shared inbox and scale your reach with AI without losing the personal touch.


Here’s what sets it apart:


- **One number your whole team can answer.** Calls can ring multiple team members at once, and the first person to pick up takes it while everyone else sees who did. You can also set up ring groups to prioritize incoming calls to reach specific colleagues. Here’s[how to share a business number with your team](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-share-a-business-phone-number-with-your-team/) .
- **Every conversation in one thread.** Calls, voicemails, notes, and[texts](https://www.quo.com/product/messaging) for each customer sit together, so whoever replies next has the full story.
- **Missed calls still get a reply — or prevent them altogether in the first place.** An[auto-reply text](https://www.quo.com/blog/texting-auto-reply-examples/) can go out right away, even if the caller hangs up without leaving a voicemail. Sona, Quo’s AI agent, can also answer, take details, and leave a summary in the inbox. 10 Sona calls per month are included.
- **Easy to scale as your team grows.** You can add users anytime, give each their own US, Canadian, or toll-free number, and[share existing numbers](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-share-a-business-phone-number-with-your-team/) so teammates can field calls and[texts](https://www.quo.com/product/messaging) together. Plus, texting is unlimited in the US and Canada on every plan.


#### ****Choose Quo if…****


Quo is the best small business phone system for teams that want:


- **Unlimited calling and texting to the US and Canada.** Quo also has affordable international[rates](https://www.quo.com/rates) .
- **Collaboration features built in.** Shared numbers,[internal threads](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/team-collaboration/internal-threads) , and[Tasks](https://www.quo.com/product/task-management) let a team cover calls and texts together instead of in silos.
- **Dozens of ways to save time through AI.**[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) , Quo’s AI voice agent, answers calls when you can’t. AI call summaries and transcripts replace manual notes, and contact suggestions keep your address book up to date. You can also integrate Quo with[ChatGPT](https://www.quo.com/integrations/chatgpt) and[Claude](https://www.quo.com/integrations/claude) to surface insights and speed up tasks like bulk texting.
- **Top-rated support and ease of use.** Quo is rated[#1 in customer satisfaction](https://www.g2.com/best-software-companies/highest-satisfaction) for VoIP providers on G2 and is consistently praised for fast onboarding.
- **9,000+ integrations.** Connect with[Slack](https://www.quo.com/integrations/slack) ,[HubSpot](https://www.quo.com/integrations/hubspot) ,[Salesforce](https://www.quo.com/integrations/salesforce) ,[Jobber](https://www.quo.com/integrations/jobber) ,[Zapier](https://www.quo.com/integrations/zapier) ,[Make](https://www.quo.com/integrations/make) , and more.


#### **Quo is not for you if you need to:**


- **Verify online accounts via 2FA.** Like with nearly all VoIP providers, you can’t use a virtual number like Quo’s to authenticate accounts with companies like Google or Uber.


Don’t worry about sitting on hold or visiting a store to activate your business phone system. With Quo, you can sign up online and get up and running in under 15 minutes. Try Quo for seven days[by signing up for our free trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) .


#### **Quo** **pricing**


Quo offers three transparent pricing plans:


- **Starter:** $15 per user per month for one local or toll-free number, unlimited calling and messaging to the US and Canada, voicemail transcripts, on-demand call recording, Zapier and Make integrations, and 10 free calls with Sona AI agent
- **Business:** $23 per user per month to access phone menus with IVR,[call transfers](https://www.quo.com/product/call-forwarding/call-transfer) , analytics, CRM integrations,[Claude](https://www.quo.com/integrations/claude) and[ChatGPT](https://www.quo.com/integrations/chatgpt) connectors, automatic call recording, and live chat support
- **Scale:** $35 per user per month for AI call tags, dedicated onboarding, inbound phone support, and priority chat and email support


For more than 10 calls a month, you can purchase additional Sona credits. These are more predictable than per-minute pricing, which can easily spike your bill when customers need more help over the phone.


Here’s what to expect from Sona’s bundled pricing:


Tier 1 Tier 2 Tier 3 Tier 4 Tier 5


Sona tiers Free $25 per month $49 per month $99 per month $199 per month


Included credits 1,000 credits/10 calls 4,000 credits/40 calls 10,000 credits/100 calls 25,000 credits/250 calls 60,000 credits/600 calls


Overage rate per call $1.00 $0.75 $0.65 $0.55 $0.45

### **2. Allo: Best for mobile-first, small teams**


Allo is a newer phone system for sales teams. It’s not quite as established as other small business phone systems on this list. But it gives you one business number per user, unlimited national calls, and unlimited inbound SMS. Plans for teams also inlcude free outbound SMS to US numbers.


Here’s what sets it apart:


- **Native CRM integrations.** Allo connects directly to HubSpot, Salesforce, and Attio, so call details live in the contact record instead of a separate app.
- **AI transcripts and summaries** . On Allo, these are available from the base plan. But Allo only stores them for 30 days, so if you need to keep call records for compliance or training, you have to export them yourself.
- **Affordable solo plan** . For $10 a month, a solopreneur can get a single business number, unlimited national calling, and unlimited inbound SMS; at the time of writing, this plan is set to launch soon
- **A power-dialer as an add-on** . Allo’s power dialer works through a call list, one number at a time. This way, outbound reps skip the manual dialing. It costs a flat $50 per month on team plans.


#### **Choose Allo if….**


Allo is a solid choice if:


- **You’re a solopreneur and want a no-frills solution** . If you just want a number to stay in touch with customers by phone, Allo is a solid, mobile-first choice.
- **Your sales team communicates with customers abroad.** Allo claims to provide virtual numbers in 85+ countries. This can help you establish a local presence and trust in your target country. Just know that most regional numbers are voice-only and don’t allow texting.
- **You make outbound sales calls all day.** Allo has features like a parallel dialer on its most expensive plan and a power dialer add-on that supports cold calling.


#### **Skip Allo if….**


Consider[Allo alternatives](https://www.quo.com/blog/allo-alternatives/) if:


- **You’re a text-first team** . Allo’s solo plan doesn’t support outbound texting. On its team plans, sending texts is only included in the US. If you’re texting in other countries, like Canada, you’ll have to pay $5 per user per month, then purchase SMS credits as you go, based on the destination.
- **You need to keep call records for compliance or training.** Since Allo’s Solo plan only stores AI transcripts and summaries for 30 days, you’re in charge of saving them. This can get old fast if you need records for audits, coaching, or customer disputes.
- **You need a call flow you can fine-tune.** Allo offers IVR menus, but[reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/the-mobile-first-company-allo/reviews/allo-review-12497691) say it lacks finer control over settings and options. If you run several departments, after-hours rules, or a multi-step menu, test how far the setup goes in the trial before you commit.


#### Allo pricing


**


You have three Allo pricing plans to choose from:


- **Solo:** $10 per month for one user, unlimited national calls, one number, call recording, AI call summaries and transcripts, and email support; at the time of writing, this plan isn’t publicly available
- **Business:** $32 per user per month for unlimited users with one number each, CRM sync with call tags in HubSpot, Pipedrive, Attio, and Salesforce, SMS support, custom AI summary templates, AI post-call actions, call analytics, and MCP connectors with Claude and ChatGPT
- **Ultra:** $100 per user per month for AI agents like the AI SDR, AI CRM manager, and AI sales coach, custom analytics dashboards, a custom AI voice for IVR, Slack support, a dedicated account manager, and custom onboarding


The AI receptionist costs $32 per agent per month, or the price of a Business user seat, to answer inbound calls.


#### **Demo**


### **3. Google Voice: Best phone service for small business using Google tools**


[Google Voice for Business](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-for-business/) is a popular small business phone system for businesses that already use products like Gmail and Google Docs. You can call and text with[Google Voice](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-alternatives/) on your existing computer, smartphone, tablet, or compatible desk phone.


Here’s what makes Google Voice stand out:


- **Easily bring together other Google apps.** Calendar, Meet, Gmail, and Contacts all connect without extra setup.
- **An affordable entry point.** Paid plans start at $10 per user per month, and it’s free for personal use.
- **Simple setup** . Users find Google Voice relatively[easy to set up](https://www.g2.com/products/google-voice/reviews/google-voice-review-12606568) and get started with.


#### **Choose Google Voice if…**


Choose Google Voice if:


- **You want unlimited US calling and texting.** You get unlimited calls and texts in the US and calls to Canada from the US.
- **You’re a one-person business that wants a simple, affordable business number.** You can get started with only $10 per month.
- **Your team already pays for Google Workspace.** That’s because team plans require a Google Workspace subscription.
- **You want to have local numbers in more than just the US or Canada.** Google Voice is available in 14+ countries.


#### **Skip Google Voice if…**


You’ll be better off with a Google Voice alternative if:


- **You want to text outside the US** . Texting works in the US only.
- **You need toll-free numbers** . Google Voice doesn’t support toll-free numbers, and you can’t port one in.
- **You want your business phone system to integrate with your tools** .[Google Voice’s integrations](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-integrations/) are limited to Google’s tools. So if you have a CRM like HubSpot, you can’t set up an integration. You’ll have to transfer your information manually, which takes time and increases the risk of errors.
- **You need time-saving AI features** . Its AI covers spam blocking and voicemail transcription. You can also use Gemini to transcribe and summarize calls. But it offers nothing beyond that, like call tagging or an AI receptionist.


#### Google Voice pricing


**


There are four[Google Voice plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-pricing/) to choose from. If you have more than one person on your team, you’ll need to have a Google Workspace subscription starting at $7 per user per month in addition to paid plan:


- **Starter with voice only** : $10 per user per month for one user, free calls in the US and Canada, and access to mobile and web apps
- **Starter** : $10 per user per month for calls to the US and Canada, voicemail transcriptions, and integrations with Google Workspace
- **Standard** : $20 per user per month to unlock on-demand call recordings, ring groups, and phone menus
- **Premier** : $30 per user per month to unlock automatic call recordings and advanced reporting


### **3. Dialpad: **Best small business phone system for call monitoring****


[Dialpad](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-alternatives/) is an AI-powered business phone solution best known for real-time transcription and live coaching. It works on your computer, smartphone, tablet, or compatible desk phone.


Two things define it:


- **AI is the core product:** Live transcription and real-time analytics are included rather than bolted on.
- **International local numbers** are available in over 50 countries.


#### **What we like about Dialpad**


- **Unlimited calling:** Calls to the US and Canada are unlimited on the base plan.
- **Video and integrations:** Dialpad includes unlimited video conferencing and broad native integrations.


#### **What we don’t like about Dialpad**


- **Features gated behind higher tiers:** Additional numbers, international SMS, and CRM integrations require an upgrade.
- **Support and setup friction:** We noticed slow support and a steep learning curve during testing, and admin setup takes longer than competitors.
- **Not ideal for very small teams:** Dialpad is better suited to teams of ~10 or more.


#### Dialpad pricing


**


Here’s how[Dialpad pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-pricing/) plans currently breakdown:


- **Standard:** $15 per user per month for free calling in the US and Canada, team messaging, and up to 250 outbound text messages
- **Pro:** $25 per user per month for additional local or international numbers, international SMS, and access to the open API and webhooks
- **Enterprise:** Get a custom quote for unlimited ring groups, unlimited office locations, and 100% uptime


### **4. Vonage: **Best small business phone solution with an API offering****


[Vonage](https://www.quo.com/blog/vonage-alternatives/) is a legacy business VoIP service provider. It’s well-known but fairly out-of-date compared to modern options like Quo and Dialpad. It offers desk-phone compatibility plus desktop, web, and mobile apps.


What stands out is its API offering for teams that want to build custom communication workflows.


#### **What we like about Vonage**


- **Unlimited calling:** All plans include unlimited calling.
- **Free number porting:** You can bring your existing numbers over at no cost.


#### **What we don’t like about Vonage**


- **Requires upgrades for today’s essentials:** Features like auto-attendants and voicemail transcriptions come standard on most other providers’ plans.
- **Add-on fees stack up fast:** Call recording runs ~$49.99 per month and toll-free numbers ~$39.99 per month extra.
- **Limited auto-replies:** Auto-reply capabilities are minimal compared to other[remote phone systems.](https://www.quo.com/blog/remote-phone-systems/)
- **Pricing penalizes small teams:** The fewer users you have, the more you pay per line.


#### Vonage pricing


**


[Vonage’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/vonage-pricing/) for their base plans depends on the size of your team, with smaller teams paying more per user. Here’s how much teams of 1-4 users can expect to pay:


- **Mobile:** $13.99 per line per month for unlimited team messaging, access to the mobile and desktop apps, and the Vonage App Center with 20 integrations
- **Premium:** $20.99 per line per month for unlimited video meetings with up to 100 participants, multilevel auto-attendants, and integrations with IP desk phones, including Cisco and similar brands
- **Advanced:** $27.99 per line per month for visual voicemail,[call groups](https://www.quo.com/blog/call-group/) , and 15 hours on-demand call recording


Learn more about how[Quo and Vonage compare](https://www.quo.com/compare/quo-vs-vonage) .


### ****5. Grasshopper: Best small business phone service for multi-digit extensions****


[Grasshopper](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-alternatives/) offers the basics like[business phone numbers](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-business-phone-number/) and extensions. You can call and text with Grasshopper on your existing computer, cell phone, or tablet.


The defining traits:


- **Prices by phone number rather than by user** , which can be cheaper for a team sharing one number.
- **A basics-only feature set** with phone numbers, extensions, voicemail — no AI or integrations.


#### **What we like about Grasshopper**


- **Unlimited US & Canada calling:** Calls and texts to the US and Canada are included.
- **Voicemail transcription:** Plans include voicemail transcription and a phone menu with extensions.


#### **What we don’t like about Grasshopper**


- **Feels dated:** We tested out Grasshopper’s admin portal and found it to be limited and hard to customize.
- **No real integrations:** There are no CRM, Slack, or Zapier integrations and no call summaries.
- **Hidden costs:** Calls to Alaska and[Hawaii](https://www.quo.com/local-numbers/hawaii) are treated as “offshore.” They require international calling and a $500 deposit.
- **Support complaints:** Slow, unhelpful support is a common theme across review sites.


#### Grasshopper pricing


**


[Grasshopper’s plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-pricing/) are different from most other small business phone systems. Instead of charging by the user, you pay based on how many phone numbers you need:


- **True Solo:** $14 per month for one phone number, one user, and one extension
- **Solo Plus:** $25 per month for one phone number, unlimited users, three extensions, call recording, IVR, and simultaneous ring
- **Small Business:** $55 per month for four phone numbers, unlimited users, unlimited extensions, and everything in Solo Plus


*Additional numbers cost $9 per month.


### **6. Nextiva: Best phone system for small business using Microsoft products**


Nextiva is a popular[VoIP service provider](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-voip-service/) that many well-known enterprises use. You can use Nextiva on your existing laptop, smartphone, tablet, or a compatible desk phone.


What makes it distinct is the communication channels. It goes beyond voice and text to unify video, social, and messaging channels like WhatsApp and Instagram in one place.


#### **What we like about Nextiva**


- **Strong collaboration and analytics:** Detailed reporting helps you keep tabs on team activity.
- **Responsive support:** Reviewers consistently praise Nextiva’s support team.
- **Unlimited calling:** Calls to the US and Canada are unlimited.


#### **What we don’t like about Nextiva**


- **Capped texting:** The base plan includes only 100 SMS per user per month.
- **Add-ons add up:** Call recording and several integrations require an upgrade or add-on fee.
- **No free trial:** Nextiva doesn’t offer a free trial.


These limitations lead many small businesses to[Nextiva alternatives](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-alternatives/) **.**


#### Nextiva pricing


**


Here’s how[Nextiva’s pricing per user](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-pricing/) breaks down:


- **Core:** $15 per user per month for voice calls, 100 text messages, team chat, voicemail transcriptions, and access to the mobile app
- **Engage:** $25 per user per month for the Microsoft Teams integration, 500 text messages, digital fax, voice analytics, 2,000 toll-free minutes, and call recording
- **Scale:** $75 per user per month for up to 100 agents for skills-based routing, IVR, call transcriptions and summaries, and API integrations


### ****7. 8×8: Best solution for global calling****


[8×8](https://www.quo.com/blog/8x8-alternatives/) is a communications platform that offers small business plans, though you can also access an enterprise-level contact center solution.


What stands out is it’s built around reach. International calling and large-scale conferencing are the reasons most teams land on it. You can use 8×8 on your existing computer, smartphone, tablet, or compatible desk phones.


#### **What we like about 8×8**


- **Large-scale conferencing:** Video and audio conferencing supports up to 500 people.
- **Broad international calling:** Unlimited calling to 14 countries makes it strong for international teams.


#### **What we don’t like about 8×8**


- **Unintuitive interface:** The platform is harder to navigate than competitors.
- **Limited recording storage:** Starter plans keep recordings for only ~30 days without an upgrade.
- **US & Canada-only SMS:** Texting is limited to the US and Canada, and[group texting](https://www.quo.com/product/messaging/group-texting) to US & Canadian numbers.


#### 8×8 pricing


**


[8×8’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/8x8-pricing/) isn’t listed online. You’ll have to contact their sales team and request a quote.


### ****8. GoTo Connect: Best small business phone software with conference bridge****


[GoTo Connect](https://www.quo.com/blog/goto-connect-alternatives/) consolidates businesses’ internal and external communication on a single platform. It offers customers a VoIP phone, virtual meeting system, ring groups, and integrations with Zoho and Zendesk. It runs on a computer, smartphone, tablet, or compatible desk phone.


#### **What we like about GoTo Connect**


- **Free international calls:** The base offering includes free calls to 50 countries.
- **Office-suite integrations:** GoTo Connect integrates with Google Workspace and Microsoft Outlook.
- **Bundled meetings:** Meetings and conferencing come alongside the phone system.


#### **What we don’t like about GoTo Connect**


- **Shared inbox is gated:** It isn’t available on the base plan.
- **Capped toll-free minutes:** Minutes are pooled and capped at 1,000 across plans, and overages get pricey.
- **Limited texting:** SMS and MMS is restricted to the US and Canada.


#### GoTo Connect pricing


**


[GoTo Connect’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/goto-connect-pricing/) isn’t publicly available, but you can still see its tiers and features on the website:


- **Phone System:** Video meetings, team chat, SMS and MMS, Microsoft Teams integration, and free calls to 50 countries
- **Connect CX:** Social media integrations, shared inboxes, and AI-powered call summaries
- **Contact Center:** Auto-queue callback, advanced call routing, and call monitoring tools


### ****9. Zoom Phone: Best small business phone system for large industry events****


Zoom might be better known for its online meeting platform, but in 2019, the company broke into the VoIP phone space. Most teams pick it for its tight integration with Zoom Meetings. You can transfer from a call straight into a Zoom meeting.


#### **What we like about Zoom Phone**


- **Core features included:** Voicemail transcription, shared numbers, and call recording all come standard.
- **Coaching tools:** Call listening and whispering support live coaching.
- **Industry events capability:** You can host meetings with 100-300+ participants, depending on your plan.


#### **What we don’t like about Zoom Phone**


- **Metered base plan:** Outbound calls are metered on the entry plan.
- **Limited texting:** Repeat or automated texts require API work.
- **Heavy admin setup:** Getting a team up and running takes a lot of time, which is overkill for very small teams.
- **No free trial:**[Zoom Phone](https://www.quo.com/blog/zoom-phone-alternatives/) has no trial, and advanced analytics cost extra.


#### Zoom Phone pricing


**


[Zoom plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/zoom-phone-pricing/) have the most complicated pricing. In addition to a half dozen potential add-on fees, you can choose between these plans for a Zoom Phone:


- **Metered** : $10.50 per user per month for metered domestic calling, SMS and MMS in the US and Canada, auto-attendant, and Zoom meetings
- **Regional unlimited** : $16 per user per month for unlimited outbound calls in the US and Canada, metered international calling, and AI call summaries
- **Global Select** : $25 per user per month for unlimited calling in 40+ countries, a direct dial number, and everything in US & Canada Unlimited


You can also bundle Zoom Phone with Zoom Workplace at a discounted rate:


- **Pro Plus** : $20.50 per user per month for access to Zoom Workplace Pro, plus everything in the Unlimited plan
- **Business Plus:** $24.50 per user per month for access to Zoom Workspace, Business, visitor management tools, real-time reporting dashboards, and access to international calling add-ons


### ****10. RingCentral: Best small business phone service with desk phone rental options****


[RingCentral](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-alternatives/) has been around since 1999. Its RingEx product provides companies with business and toll-free numbers. It runs on your existing computer, mobile device, tablet, or a compatible desk phone.


Most teams choose it because it offers a full enterprise UCaaS suite with integrations and desk phone rental options.


#### **What we like about RingCentral**


- **Unlimited calling:** Calls to the US and Canada are unlimited.
- **Local and toll-free numbers:** RingCentral provides both.
- **Deep integrations:** It connects with Slack, Microsoft 365, Salesforce, and Zendesk — with an upgrade.


#### **What we don’t like about RingCentral**


- **Major texting limits:** The base plan includes only 25 texts per user per month.
- **Call recording limits:** Automatic call recordings are available only after upgrading
- **Message storage cap:** A ~[5,000-text-per-user](https://support.ringcentral.com/mvp/admin/company-account-settings/ringcentral-data-retention-policies.html) cap can be a problem for record-keeping or disputes.
- **Support gaps:** Reviewers report poor support.


#### RingCentral pricing


**


Here’s how[RingCentral pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-pricing/) break down:


- **Core:** $20 per user per month to access unlimited domestic calling, SMS and MMS, and IVR
- **Advanced:** $25 per user per month to access auto call recording, advanced call monitoring and handling, and multi-site management
- **Ultra:** $35 per user per month to access unlimited enterprise-grade HD video, whiteboards, messaging, customizable business insights, and unlimited file-sharing with storage for files and recordings


##


3 key reasons to use a VoIP phone system for small businesses


**


While some of these small business phone systems can connect to desk phones, they’re all virtual phone systems. Here are the reasons thousands of businesses go with this solution.


### **1. Works from anywhere on any device**


Since a small business virtual phone service only requires an internet connection, you and your team can work from almost anywhere. Whether you’re a solopreneur who frequently travels, a business with team members[in the Philippines](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-call-philippines-from-us/) , or a company that’s opening up new locations, your virtual business phone system can travel with you.


Shared numbers also allow you to[share a single number with team members internationally](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/members#adding-team-members) . This means that a virtual assistant can call and text clients from your number — even while across the globe. Your distributed team can all share responsibility for a single phone number.


### **2. Scales with your team as you grow**


[The best virtual phone systems](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-virtual-phone-services/) charge companies by the user. ****Frequently asked questions about small business phone systems****


If you still have questions about small business phone systems as you consider making a switch, check out our answers to these frequently asked questions.


****What is a small business phone system?****


A small business phone system lets you manage your business communications over calls and texts whether you’re a solopreneur or a growing team. The best systems act similarly to email inboxes. This makes it easy for you to review a conversation’s history and focus on building relationships with your customers.


****How much does a small business phone system cost?****


Small[business phone system costs](https://www.quo.com/blog/business-phone-system-cost/) vary depending on the service you select, the type of business phone system you use, and how many users you have.
A starting plan for[VoIP phone](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-does-voip-work/) systems costs $15 to $25 per user per month. Mid-range softphone systems cost $25 to $50 per user per month.
If you opt for an on-premises PBX system, it will cost between $500 to $1,000 per user. And an analog PBX phone system will cost $1000 to $2,000 for a five-person team.


**What are the best free small business phone systems?**


Truly free small business phone systems don’t really exist. Most free options, like Google Voice for personal use or TextNow, are designed for individual use and lack core business features like call routing, CRM integrations, and workflow automations. They tend to work fine for solo freelancers but most growing businesses will outgrow them quickly.


If you want to test a real business phone system before committing, Quo offers a[free seven-day trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) .


**Do I need an IT person to set up a small business phone system?**


Traditional business phone systems, like landlines, require hardware to be installed and the help of IT professionals. However, VoIP makes this easier. To set up a small business phone system, you can just sign up online and invite your team members through email. It only takes a few minutes!


**Do I need to buy special hardware or desk phones to use Quo?**


No, you can use Quo’s virtual phone numbers on your existing smartphone, tablet, laptop, or desktop computer.


****What are the benefits of a cloud-based office phone system?****


Cloud phone systems offer advanced calling features and business app integrations that are only possible with an internet connection. And they come at a far lower price than traditional phones. Plus, with easy upgrades and no need for brand new devices, scaling your small business is simple.


**What is a PBX system for small business?**


A PBX or[private branch exchange](https://www.quo.com/blog/pbx-phone-system/) is a phone system that lets businesses manage calls between employees and route incoming and outgoing calls through shared lines — rather than giving every employee their own separate phone line.


PBX solutions can either manage calls through the PSTN network, or they can use VoIP technology to manage calls over the internet. This is called IP-PBX. These systems require expensive hardware, proprietary office phones, and on-site expertise to maintain, but they can provide advanced calling features.


**Do businesses still use landlines?**


Mostly no. While traditional analog landlines were once the standard, most businesses have moved to modern phone solutions that offer better features. Though landlines were reliable and produced great call quality, these phone systems were costly to set up and maintain.


Analog systems are still used in some large institutions and areas without reliable internet access, where they’re managed through key service units, or KSUs.

Many small business owners start off by using their[personal cell phone numbers for business](https://www.quo.com/blog/using-personal-phone-for-work/) — but you should avoid that. Adding a virtual business number to your personal phone, however, sidesteps many of those problems:

**Is it better to have a separate business phone?**


If you’re considering a virtual business number, you may be wondering if there’s any downside to *not* having a[separate business phone](https://www.quo.com/blog/add-business-line-to-cell-phone/) — whether a separate cell phone or a landline.


One downside that VoIP services have is that they generally don’t support emergency services like authentication codes via text. Most VoIP platforms share this problem. For fraud prevention reasons, companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you use a VoIP number to authenticate accounts through them.
